label: def:spectator-normalization
title: Spectator normalization factor
html:
Definition. Spectator normalization factor

The spectator normalization captures the contribution of unchanged nucleons to the Q-value character sum. In a beta decay, one neutron converts to a proton. The remaining Z protons and N - 1 neutrons act as spectators.

1. Definition. The spectator normalization factor is

  S(Z, N-1) = a^{Z} \cdot b^{N-1}

where a = -h/2 and b = -3(q^2-1)(q^2+1)^2/(4q^3) are the channel sums of the per-nucleon Garside factors.

2. Fermionic character. Both a < 0 and b < 0 for all q > 1. This negativity reflects the fermionic character of the nucleon. The sign of the spectator product is (-1)^{A-1}. This sign fixes the parity regime for the Q-value.
